# ggguides

*rearranging the legends on a ggplot*

ggguides places, styles and combines the legends of
[ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org) plots with named functions,
such as
[`legend_left()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_left.md),
[`legend_inside()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_inside.md)
or
[`legend_style()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_style.md),
each added to a plot with `+`.

Each function sets the ggplot2 theme and guide options that belong to
one change together, for a legend on the left its position, its
justification and the alignment of the legend boxes, and returns an
ordinary ggplot2 component that combines with the rest of the plot’s
theme. For layouts of several plots,
[`collect_legends()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/collect_legends.md)
and
[`shared_legend()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/shared_legend.md)
edit the gtable, the table of graphical objects that ggplot2 draws, so
that one legend remains. You choose where each legend goes and how it
looks, one aesthetic at a time when a plot has several. ggguides
supports:

- **Placement.**
  [`legend_left()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_left.md),
  [`legend_right()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_right.md),
  [`legend_top()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_top.md)
  and
  [`legend_bottom()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_bottom.md)
  move the legend to a side,
  [`legend_inside()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/reference/legend_inside.html)
  into a corner or to `x`/`y` coordinates, and
  [`legend_none()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_none.md)
  removes it.
- **Styling.**
  [`legend_style()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/reference/legend_style.html)
  sets size, font, background, border and margins.
  [`legend_wrap()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_wrap.md)
  arranges the keys in columns or rows,
  [`legend_reverse()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_reverse.md)
  and
  [`legend_order()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_order.md)
  set the order of the entries, and
  [`colorbar_style()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/colorbar_style.md)
  styles continuous scales.
- **Several legends on one plot.** The `by` argument of every placement
  and style function targets one aesthetic.
  [`legend_hide()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_hide.md)
  and
  [`legend_select()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_select.md)
  drop or keep legends by aesthetic, and
  [`legend_order_guides()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_order_guides.md)
  sets their order.
- **One legend for several plots.**
  [`collect_legends()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/collect_legends.md)
  and
  [`collect_axes()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/collect_axes.md)
  remove duplicates from a
  [patchwork](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com) layout,
  [`shared_legend()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/shared_legend.md)
  arranges plots with one legend without patchwork, and
  [`get_legend()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/get_legend.md)
  extracts a legend for [cowplot](https://wilkelab.org/cowplot/) or
  grid.

## Installation

``` r

install.packages("ggguides")
```

Development version:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("gcol33/ggguides")
```

## Usage

1.  Build the plot with ggplot2.
2.  Add a placement function such as
    [`legend_left()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_left.md)
    or
    [`legend_inside()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_inside.md).
3.  Add
    [`legend_style()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_style.md)
    to change how the legend looks.

``` r

library(ggplot2)
library(ggguides)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3)
p + legend_left()
```

![Scatter plot of car weight against fuel economy from mtcars, points
coloured by number of cylinders, with the colour legend on the left of
the panel.](reference/figures/README-left-1.svg)

Inside the panel, a corner is named with `position`, and the style is
added as a further layer:

``` r

p +
  legend_inside(position = "topright") +
  legend_style(size = 18, title_face = "bold")
```

![The same scatter plot with the colour legend inside the panel in the
top-right corner, its title in bold and its text
larger.](reference/figures/README-inside-1.svg)

## Compared with theme()

In ggplot2, a legend on the left with its keys aligned at the top takes
three [`theme()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html)
arguments.
[`legend_left()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_left.md)
sets them together:

``` r

p + theme(legend.position = "left",
          legend.justification.left = "top",
          legend.box.just = "left")

p + legend_left(justification = "top")
```

## Several legends on one plot

A plot with several aesthetics has one legend per aesthetic. The `by`
argument places or styles one of them and leaves the others as they are:

``` r

q <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl), size = hp)) +
  geom_point()
q + legend_top(by = "colour") + legend_right(by = "size")
```

![Scatter plot of car weight against fuel economy with points coloured
by cylinders and sized by horsepower; the colour legend is above the
panel and the size legend to its
right.](reference/figures/README-by-1.svg)

Calls with `by` add up, one line per legend and setting. [Multiple
Legends](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/multiple-legends.html#six-legends-stacked-per-side)
builds this plot with six legends, two on top, two on the right, one at
the bottom and one on the left:

![Scatter plot of car weight against fuel economy with six legends:
colour and fill above the panel, size and transparency on the right,
shape below and line type on the
left.](reference/figures/README-six-legends-1.svg)

## One legend for several plots

A patchwork layout repeats the legend of each plot.
[`collect_legends()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/collect_legends.md)
keeps one, and `span = TRUE` stretches it along the full height of
stacked plots:

``` r

library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, hp, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, disp, colour = factor(cyl))) + geom_point()
stacked <- (p1 / p2 / p3) + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1.5, 1))

gt <- collect_legends(stacked, position = "right", span = TRUE)
grid::grid.draw(gt)
```

![Three scatter plots of mtcars stacked vertically, of weight,
horsepower and displacement against fuel economy, with one colour legend
for cylinders on the right spanning all three
panels.](reference/figures/README-collect-1.svg)

With `span = 1:2` the legend sits beside rows 1 and 2 only. Without
patchwork, `shared_legend(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 1, position = "bottom")`
arranges the plots with one legend. [Patchwork
Integration](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/patchwork.html)
covers both, along with collected axes and cowplot.

## Documentation

Start with [Getting Started with
ggguides](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/getting-started.html):
placing, styling and wrapping a legend, and combining the functions on
one plot.

- [Legend
  Positioning](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/positioning.html):
  the four sides, positions inside the panel, direction and removing the
  legend.
- [Styling &
  Customization](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/styling.html):
  fonts, text rotation, backgrounds, borders, key size, wrapping, entry
  order and colour bars.
- [Multiple
  Legends](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/multiple-legends.html):
  hiding, selecting, ordering, merging and placing legends per
  aesthetic.
- [Patchwork
  Integration](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/articles/patchwork.html):
  one legend and shared axes across a layout of plots.
- [Full reference](https://gillescolling.com/ggguides/reference/): every
  function, grouped by job.

## Getting help

Questions and bug reports go to the [GitHub
issues](https://github.com/gcol33/ggguides/issues). A bug report is
easiest to act on with a small reproducible example, for instance made
with [reprex](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/).

## Acknowledgements

ggguides sets options of [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org) and
edits the plots it draws with [gtable](https://gtable.r-lib.org);
multi-plot layouts come from
[patchwork](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com).

# Package index

## Position Helpers

Control legend placement

- [`legend_left()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_left.md)
  : Place Legend on the Left with Proper Alignment
- [`legend_right()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_right.md)
  : Place Legend on the Right with Proper Alignment
- [`legend_top()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_top.md)
  : Place Legend on Top with Horizontal Layout
- [`legend_bottom()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_bottom.md)
  : Place Legend on Bottom with Horizontal Layout
- [`legend_inside()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_inside.md)
  : Place Legend Inside the Plot Area
- [`legend_none()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_none.md)
  : Remove Legend from Plot

## Direction Helpers

Control legend orientation

- [`legend_horizontal()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_horizontal.md)
  : Set Legend Direction to Horizontal
- [`legend_vertical()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_vertical.md)
  : Set Legend Direction to Vertical

## Style Helpers

Customize legend appearance

- [`legend_style()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_style.md)
  : Style Legend Appearance
- [`legend_wrap()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_wrap.md)
  : Wrap Legend Entries into Columns or Rows
- [`legend_reverse()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_reverse.md)
  : Reverse Legend Order
- [`legend_order()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_order.md)
  : Reorder Legend Entries
- [`legend_keys()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_keys.md)
  : Customize Legend Key Appearance
- [`legend_auto_fit()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_auto_fit.md)
  : Auto-fit Legend to Plot Height
- [`center_legend_title()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/center_legend_title.md)
  : Center Legend Title Over Keys
- [`colorbar_style()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/colorbar_style.md)
  [`colourbar_style()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/colorbar_style.md)
  : Style Continuous Color Bar Legends

## Multiple Legends

Control individual legends when a plot has multiple aesthetics

- [`legend_hide()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_hide.md)
  : Hide Specific Legends
- [`legend_select()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_select.md)
  : Keep Only Specific Legends
- [`legend_order_guides()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_order_guides.md)
  : Control Legend Display Order
- [`legend_merge()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_merge.md)
  : Force Legends to Merge
- [`legend_split()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/legend_split.md)
  : Force Legends to Stay Separate

## Multi-Panel Layouts

Collect and align legends across multi-panel plots (patchwork or
cowplot)

- [`collect_legends()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/collect_legends.md)
  : Collect Legends from Patchwork Compositions
- [`collect_axes()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/collect_axes.md)
  [`align_guides_h()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/collect_axes.md)
  : Collect Axes from Patchwork Compositions
- [`get_legend()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/get_legend.md)
  : Extract Legend from a ggplot
- [`shared_legend()`](https://gcol33.github.io/ggguides/reference/shared_legend.md)
  : Combine Plots with a Shared Legend
